reason: Afero's live Senior Mobile (Flutter/KMP) posting confesses the exact situation David fixes — an inherited, non-greenfield companion-app codebase for BLE connected devices used by millions, being re-architected mid-flight (Redux to Provider) while the app remains the activation path for 1,000+ shipping SKUs.

company.name: Afero, Inc.
company.one_liner: IoT platform-as-a-service that powers the connectivity, security and companion-app layer for connected consumer and industrial devices, including the Hubspace smart-home line behind brands like Defiant, Hampton Bay and EcoSmart.
company.stage: Series C (~$72-100M raised; last round $50M, Dec 2021, led by Crosspoint Capital; founded 2014); ~30-50 employees
company.hq: Los Altos, California, USA (hybrid, 3 days/week in office)

evidence_jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer — Mobile (Flutter / KMP)
evidence_jobs.quote: This is not a greenfield role, you'll inherit a mature codebase and be expected to improve it. ... You'll work on real problems: connected device onboarding over BLE, real-time device control, GraphQL API integration, and an ongoing migration from Redux to a Provider-based architecture.

evidence_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
evidence_jobs.quote: Lead program execution across diverse engineering teams (Firmware, Mobile, Cloud, and QA) to ensure seamless integration of hardware and software.

people_spec: Senior Vice President of Engineering (owns mobile, firmware and cloud teams — the hiring manager for the mobile role)
CEO & Co-founder (30-person company; founder is hands-on and mobile-native)
Chief Product and Partnerships Officer (owns the Hubspace product line the app serves)
Engineering Manager / Team Lead, Mobile (if one exists — the posting says the senior hire will mentor mid-level engineers, implying a thin mobile leadership layer)
Senior Technical Program Manager, Platform (they are hiring one to coordinate Firmware/Mobile/Cloud/QA delivery)
talk_track: I ran the mobile team behind the SharkClean app last year - 5M+ customers, nine App Store releases, BLE onboarding, and post-release crash triage on a codebase nobody had the budget to rewrite. Your Senior Mobile (Flutter/KMP) posting is unusually honest about where Hubspace sits: "This is not a greenfield role, you'll inherit a mature codebase and be expected to improve it," with a Redux-to-Provider migration already in flight. Here's the read I'd offer for free: the risk isn't the state-management rewrite, it's that this same app is the activation path for the 1,000+ SKUs the posting says run on Afero, so the release train can't pause while the architecture moves underneath it. The teams that come through it intact freeze BLE pairing and device onboarding on the old, boring path and migrate everything else first - setup is the one flow where a regression costs you a return instead of a bug report. Whoever you hire will hit that call in their third week. Which flow are you migrating last? - David Sowsy
